posts.headline: Traveling with Mom or Dad this season?
posts.subhead: A little planning makes the trip easier for everyone.
changes: Book nonstop flights when you can, travel at your parent's best time of day, and leave room for rest.
Carry-on, not checked: medications in labeled bottles plus extra days, a medication list, and insurance cards.
Call the airline ahead to request a wheelchair or boarding help. At the airport, ask any TSA officer for a Passenger Support Specialist.
On long trips, get up and move often and drink water. Ask the doctor about compression stockings.
If memory is a concern, keep routines familiar and make sure your parent carries ID and an emergency contact.
When you arrive: check for loose rugs and cords, and add a night-light on the path to the bathroom.
posts.verdict_text: Original Medicare covers care anywhere in the U.S. Medicare Advantage plans may limit out-of-network care, so call the plan before an out-of-state trip.
actions: At the airport: ask TSA for a Passenger Support Specialist
Medicare travel questions: NJ SHIP, 1-800-792-8820
Memory concerns: Alzheimer's Association, 800-272-3900
posts.caption_rendered:
Holiday travel is hard enough. Add a parent who tires easily, takes several medications or gets confused in new places, and it takes real planning.

Swipe for what to pack, how to get help at the airport, what to watch for on long drives, and the insurance question to ask before you leave.

Two numbers worth saving:
TSA Cares, 855-787-2227. Flying this week? Ask any TSA officer at the airport for a Passenger Support Specialist. For future trips, call at least 72 hours ahead.
NJ SHIP, 1-800-792-8820. Free Medicare counseling, including what's covered when you travel.

Caring for someone with memory loss? The Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline is 800-272-3900.

Sources: TSA (Passenger Support / TSA Cares); U.S. DOT, Air Carrier Access Act guidance; Medicare.gov; Alzheimer's Association, Traveling and Dementia. Last checked Nov 23, 2026. Independent, not a government office.

posts.headline: Stay NJ's income limit is now $200,000
posts.subhead: What senior homeowners should know before 2027 payments.
changes: The state budget signed June 30, 2026 cut the Stay NJ income limit from $500,000 to $200,000. Payments in 2027 go only to households at or under $200,000.

2027 maximum benefit, per year: up to $100,000 income, $6,500. $100,000 to $150,000, $5,000. $150,000 to $200,000, $4,000. Over $200,000, $0. The state says these assume no Stay NJ changes in the FY2028 budget.
Who qualifies: you or your spouse were 65 or older during 2025, you owned and lived in the home all of 2025, and the home is subject to property taxes (or P.I.L.O.T.).
Renters and mobile home owners are not eligible. Social Security disability under 65 doesn't qualify you on its own, but a married couple can qualify if one spouse is 65 or older.
posts.verdict_text: If your parent's household income is over $200,000, they shouldn't count on a Stay NJ payment in 2027. The 2025 benefit is paid in February and May 2027.
actions: Check status: nj.gov/treasury/taxation/staynj
Use the "Check 2025 Benefit Status" tool
Each applicant gets a statement with their Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ amounts

If your parent counted on Stay NJ property tax relief, the rules have changed. The state budget signed June 30 cut the income limit from $500,000 to $200,000. posts.headline: NJ state of emergency: Thanksgiving storm
posts.subhead: How to keep an older parent safe through Thursday's nor'easter.
changes: The statewide state of emergency starts at 6 p.m. tonight. The worst conditions come on Thanksgiving Day, improving Friday.
Expect wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph, 1 to 3 inches of rain, and likely power outages. Travel isn't banned, but officials urge staying off the roads.
Visiting Mom or Dad? Get there tonight or stay home Thursday. A video call beats a crash. Never drive through a flooded road.
Tonight: charge phones and medical devices, gather a week of medications and a med list, and put flashlights (not candles) by the bed.
Oxygen, CPAP or other powered equipment? Check backup batteries and tanks, and decide where your parent goes if the power stays out.
If the power goes out: never run a generator, grill or gas stove indoors or in a garage. Stay 30 feet from downed wires. Keep the fridge closed.
posts.verdict_text: Older adults who live alone or rely on powered medical equipment are most at risk when the lights go out. A plan made tonight beats one made in the dark.
actions: Report outages: PSE&G 800-436-7734 · JCP&L 888-544-4877
Local help: dial 211 · Emergencies: 911
Call a parent who lives alone Thursday AM and PM
posts.caption_rendered:

posts.headline: UMARY Hyaluronic Acid capsules recalled nationwide
posts.subhead: Hidden prescription drugs found inside supplement capsules
changes: Product contains undeclared Dexamethasone, a prescription steroid
Undeclared Diclofenac, a prescription anti-inflammatory, also found
Undeclared Omeprazole, a prescription stomach drug, also found
Marketed without an FDA-approved application; recall is ongoing
posts.verdict_text: Anyone using this supplement should stop immediately. Hidden prescription drugs can cause serious harm, especially for older adults.
actions: Stop using UMARY Acido Hialuronico 850mg capsules immediately
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before stopping any related treatment
Contact IBeautiStore.com or your retailer about returning the product
posts.caption: A Class I recall has been issued for UMARY Acido Hialuronico, also sold as New Hyaluronic Acid 850mg Sealed 30 Caps, distributed nationwide across the USA. FDA laboratory analysis found the supplement contains three undeclared prescription-strength ingredients: Dexamethasone, a steroid; Diclofenac, an anti-inflammatory; and Omeprazole, a stomach acid drug. None of these were listed on the label. The product was also marketed without an FDA-approved application. Hidden prescription drugs can interact with existing medications and are especially risky for older adults. If you or someone you care for has this product, stop using it and speak with a doctor or pharmacist right away. Source: FDA, Recall Number D-0189-2027

posts.headline: 3B Medical Recalls Luna G3 BPAP System
posts.subhead: Device may report wrong pressure readings during sleep therapy
changes: The configured IPAP value is recorded and transmitted instead of the actual delivered inspiratory pressure.
The error occurs when Targeted VT is enabled on the device.
Recall covers 12,672 units distributed nationwide, including Puerto Rico.
posts.verdict_text: Adults using the Luna G3 BPAP System for obstructive sleep apnea should check if their device is affected. Do not stop therapy without speaking to your doctor.
actions: Check if your BPAP device is the Luna G3 model LG3800-30VT.
Contact 3B Medical or your equipment provider to confirm if your unit is included.
Do not stop using your BPAP therapy without first asking your doctor or pharmacist.
posts.caption: 3B Medical has recalled the Luna G3 BPAP System, a breathing device used to treat obstructive sleep apnea in adults. The problem: when a feature called Targeted VT is turned on, the device records and transmits the pressure it was set to deliver rather than the pressure actually delivered to the patient. This means caregivers and doctors may be reviewing inaccurate data. The FDA has classified this as a Class I recall, its most serious category. About 12,672 units were distributed across the United States and Puerto Rico. If you or someone you care for uses this device, contact your equipment provider right away. Source: FDA, Recall Number Z-0409-2027.

The hidden drugs: dexamethasone (a steroid), diclofenac (a pain reliever) and omeprazole. Taken it for weeks? Call the doctor before stopping: steroids shouldn't always stop suddenly.
Sleep apnea machine: 3B Medical Luna G3 BPAP, model LG3800-30VT. 12,672 units sold nationwide.
With the Targeted VT setting on, it reports the pressure it was set to, not what it actually delivered. Don't stop therapy: call the equipment supplier and the doctor.
Hospital anesthetic: Brevital Sodium (methohexital) 500 mg vials from Par Health. Particles (cellulose) found inside; 20,567 vials shipped in the U.S. and Canada.
Hospital kits: Cardinal Health Presource kits containing BD Alaris pump infusion sets. Shipped to California, Texas and North Carolina only.
You can't buy the Brevital vials or the Cardinal kits. They're used by hospitals and clinics, which get recall notices directly.
If your parent has a procedure coming up, it's fair to ask whether the facility has checked its recalls.
posts.verdict_text: All four are Class I, the FDA's most serious recall level, for products that could cause serious health problems.
actions: Check the medicine cabinet for UMARY capsules

evidence: UMARY: IBeautiStore.com, FDA Recall D-0189-2027, Class I, listed Nov 18, 2026. Undeclared dexamethasone, diclofenac and omeprazole; marketed without approved NDA/ANDA. Distribution: USA nationwide. Status: ongoing.

Brevital: Par Health (distributed by Par Pharmaceutical, Chestnut Ridge, NY), FDA Recall D-0156-2027, Class I, listed Oct 28, 2026. Particulate matter identified as cellulose. 20,567 vials. Distribution: US nationwide and Canada. Status: ongoing.

Luna G3: 3B Medical, FDA Recall Z-0409-2027, Class I, listed Nov 18, 2026. Model LG3800-30VT, bi-level PAP for adult obstructive sleep apnea. Configured IPAP recorded and transmitted instead of delivered pressure when Targeted VT is enabled. 12,672 units, US nationwide incl. Puerto Rico. Ongoing.

Cardinal Health 200: Presource PBDS kits containing BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets (Pump Module 8100), FDA Recalls Z-0329-2027 and Z-0330-2027, Class I, listed Nov 18, 2026. Reason: notification of performance disclosures of kit component. 30,137 kits; 9,571 units. Distribution: CA, TX, NC. Ongoing.

Four Class I recalls, the FDA's most serious level. Two could be in your parent's home. Two are hospital products worth knowing about.

UMARY Acido Hialuronico 850 mg capsules, sold online by IBeautiStore.com, contain prescription drugs that aren't on the label: dexamethasone, a steroid; diclofenac, a pain reliever; and omeprazole. 3B Medical's Luna G3 BPAP sleep apnea machine (model LG3800-30VT) can report the pressure it was set to instead of what it actually delivered when the Targeted VT setting is on. Don't stop therapy. Call the equipment supplier and the doctor.

Par Health is recalling 20,567 vials of the anesthetic Brevital Sodium after particles were found inside, and Cardinal Health is recalling procedure kits with BD Alaris infusion sets shipped to California, Texas and North Carolina. posts.headline: Home for Thanksgiving? Notice gently.
posts.subhead: A visit can make slow changes easier to spot.
changes: Around the house: little or expired food, unopened mail or unpaid bills, more clutter, missed or mixed-up medications.
Health and getting around: noticeable weight change, falls or trouble walking, clothes that don't suit the weather.
Memory and mood: memory slips that disrupt daily life, trouble with familiar tasks, confusion about the day, mood changes.
These can have other causes, like depression, infection or medications. A doctor's visit is the right first step.
One sign isn't a verdict. Jot down what you noticed and compare notes with siblings after the holiday, not at the table.
Start small: pick a quiet moment, ask instead of accuse, and offer one practical help, like grocery delivery or a ride.
posts.verdict_text: Talking early, while your parent can help decide, keeps more options open: help at home, adult day, respite care or assisted living.
actions: Free NJ help: 877-222-3737 (your county ADRC)
Memory concerns: Alzheimer's Association 24/7, 800-272-3900
Save this for the drive home
posts.caption_rendered:
Thanksgiving is often the first time in months that families are all in one room. If something about Mom or Dad seems different this year, you're not imagining it, and you're not alone.

Swipe for what to notice and how to start the conversation, gently. One change doesn't mean a crisis. It means it's time to pay attention, compare notes with family, and plan the next talk.

November is National Family Caregivers Month. If you're already helping a parent, you're a caregiver too.

posts.headline: Your parent's 2027 Medicare and Social Security numbers
posts.subhead: Both changes are final and start in January.
changes: Social Security benefits rise 3.6% in January 2027. The average retirement benefit goes up about $75 a month.
The standard Medicare Part B premium rises to $209.40 a month, up $6.50 from $202.90.
The Part B deductible rises to $292 (from $283). The Part A hospital deductible is $1,776 per benefit period.
If your parent has a my Social Security account, the 2027 COLA notice is already in the Message Center. Paper notices arrive by mail in December.
posts.verdict_text: Part B usually comes out of the Social Security check, so the raise your parent actually sees will be a little smaller than 3.6%. Higher-income beneficiaries pay more for Part B.
actions: Check the new amount in my Social Security
Paper COLA notices arrive by mail in December
Free Medicare help: NJ SHIP, 1-800-792-8820

posts.headline: Recall: about 338,800 DREO space heaters
posts.subhead: They can overheat and catch fire.
changes: Model DR-HSH015: a black ceramic heater, about 11.5 inches wide by 13 inches tall, with a remote.
Only units made April 2025 through January 2026. Check the label underneath for date codes 2025/04 to 2026/01.
Sold at Costco and online at Dreo.com, Best Buy, Kohl's, Lowe's, QVC, Home Depot and others, $70 to $110.
DREO received 17 reports of the heaters igniting, including 3 with property damage and 1 burn injury.
posts.verdict_text: Stop using a recalled heater now. DREO offers a free replacement: you'll be asked to unplug it, cut the cord and send a photo.
actions: Call DREO: 833-820-0887 (8:30-6 ET, Mon-Fri)
Or dreo.com → Product Recalls
Full details: cpsc.gov, Recall 27-054
posts.caption_rendered:
If your parent keeps a small heater by the chair or bed, check it this weekend. DREO is recalling about 338,800 DR-HSH015 space heaters because they can overheat and ignite.

Flip the heater over: if the model is DR-HSH015 and the date code is between 2025/04 and 2026/01, stop using it and contact DREO for a free replacement.

For any space heater this winter: plug it straight into the wall (not an extension cord), keep it 3 feet from beds, curtains and papers, turn it off when leaving the room or going to sleep, and make sure smoke alarms work.

Source: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, DREO space heater recall, Oct 29, 2026. Last checked Nov 23, 2026. Independent, not a government office.

posts.headline: Scams against older adults: the new FTC numbers
posts.subhead: What the report found, and a simple plan to make with your parent.
changes: Adults 60+ reported about $3 billion in fraud losses in 2025. The FTC estimates the true cost may be far higher.

Warning signs: urgency, secrecy, and payment by gift card, wire, crypto or cash handed to a courier.

actions: Agree on a family code word
Ask your parent to call you before sending money
Report it: ReportFraud.ftc.gov

posts.headline: Caregivers need breaks too
posts.subhead: That's what respite care is for.
changes: Respite care is short-term care for your parent so you can rest, run errands, work or travel.
It can be a few hours or a few days: an aide at home, an adult day program, or a short stay in a care facility.
NJ's Statewide Respite Care Program helps eligible families with respite costs.
It has financial eligibility rules. Your county office can tell you whether your family qualifies.
posts.verdict_text: Taking a break isn't giving up. Rested caregivers give better care, and stay caregivers longer.

posts.headline: Facility Check: choosing a North Jersey nursing home?
posts.subhead: Three public records to check first.
changes: Care Compare star ratings: Medicare.gov/care-compare rates every Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing home on inspections, staffing and quality. Look at each rating, not just the overall stars.
Inspection reports: on the same page, open the inspection results. Look for deficiencies marked as harm or "immediate jeopardy," and problems that repeat year after year.
The Special Focus Facility list: CMS publishes a monthly list of nursing homes with a history of serious quality problems, plus candidates that qualify but haven't been selected.
Then visit more than once, including a mealtime or evening. Watch how staff talk with residents and how quickly call lights are answered.
posts.verdict_text: If something's wrong after move-in, the NJ Long-Term Care Ombudsman investigates concerns for residents 60+. Complaints are confidential, and anonymous complaints are accepted. In an emergency, call 911.

posts.headline: Holidays when a parent has dementia
posts.subhead: Small changes can make the season easier for everyone.
changes: Keep the routine: usual mealtimes and bedtimes, and visits at your parent's best time of day.
Smaller is better: fewer guests, less noise, shorter visits, and a quiet room they can go to.
Prepare guests ahead of time. Suggest they introduce themselves and keep conversation simple.
Include them with a familiar, simple job: folding napkins, stirring, or looking at old photos together.
posts.verdict_text: New faces, noise and changed routines can be overwhelming for someone living with dementia. A few adjustments help them, and help you.

posts.headline: Look up any nursing home before you visit
posts.subhead: Four checks that take under ten minutes.
changes: Check the 1-to-5 star rating: it combines health inspections, staffing, and quality measures in one score.
Read the last three years of health inspection reports to see citations, what was wrong, and whether it was fixed.
Check staffing: look for nurse hours per resident per day and staff turnover — more hours, less turnover is better.
Look for any Medicare penalties — a fine or denied payment — listed on the facility's Care Compare page.
posts.verdict_text: A quick Care Compare search before you visit can reveal inspection citations, low staffing, or Medicare penalties that a tour alone will not show.
actions: Search any NJ nursing home free at medicare.gov/care-compare

Before you tour a nursing home in Bergen, Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, or Warren County, spend a few minutes on Care Compare. CAREGIVER TOOLKIT

If your aging parent has Medicare questions, a free expert is a phone call away. NJ SHIP — the State Health Insurance Assistance Program — places trained volunteer counselors in all eight North Jersey counties: Bergen, Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, and Warren. They help with everything from choosing between Original Medicare and an Advantage plan, to untangling a denied claim, to finding programs that lower prescription costs. Counselors do not sell insurance and do not steer you toward any company or plan. Appointments are available by phone, video, or in person. Call 1-800-792-8820 weekdays between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm to reach the NJ Division of Aging Services State Health Insurance Assistance Program.

posts.headline: NJ's two drug programs: which one fits you
posts.subhead: Income limits, copays, and how to apply
changes: PAAD: NJ residents 65+, 2026 income under $54,943 (single)/$62,390 (married); $5 generic, $7 brand-name copays.
Senior Gold: income $54,943–$64,943 (single) or $62,390–$72,390 (married); copay $15 + 50% of remaining cost.
Senior Gold caps costs at $2,000 (single) or $3,000 (married); after that, you pay $15 per prescription.
PAAD pays Part D premiums, deductibles, and donut hole gaps; Part D enrollment required if Medicare-eligible.
posts.verdict_text: Either program can cut a parent's drug costs dramatically. Knowing which one fits your income is the first step to saving.
actions: Call the PAAD/Senior Gold hotline: 1-800-792-9745
Apply online at nj.gov/humanservices/doas/services/l-p/njsave/ (NJSave application)
Ask your pharmacist whether your current Part D plan qualifies for PAAD premium coverage
posts.caption_rendered:
BENEFITS, EXPLAINED

New Jersey offers two state-funded programs that lower prescription drug costs for older adults and people with disabilities. PAAD is designed for those with lower incomes and caps copays at $5 for generics and $7 for brand-name drugs. Senior Gold, for those just above the PAAD income limit, charges $15 plus half the remaining cost but protects you with a yearly out-of-pocket cap. Both programs work alongside Medicare Part D, and assets are not counted for eligibility. If you are caring for an aging parent in Bergen, Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, or Warren County, a quick call or online application could mean hundreds of dollars in savings. Source: NJ Division of Aging Services.
